- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid downward overshoot.  
- Model often overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +1.00 sentiment) by overshooting true price — cap forecast at +10–15% above recent peak if sentiment is strong.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting — apply a “sentiment pivot” correction: add 2–5% to forecast from pivot point onward.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price in 70% of cases when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 3–5% baseline offset if sentiment is ≤ 0.33.
